primary.predictor: log1p effective colony number at census year t
primary.baseline: island fixed effects + current log1p abundance + year

active_colony_count.interpretation: directionally positive coefficient but no held-out-year predictive improvement

add_previous_growth.interpretation: primary effective-colony signal persists after adding demographic momentum

four_persistently_extant_islands.interpretation: signal is not driven by Litchfield extinction/post-extinction structure

supported: Within-island breeding-colony structure contains small but positive held-out-year information about next-year island demographic growth beyond current abundance, island identity and secular year trend.
The predeclared effective-colony-number coefficient is positive and the full model improves leave-one-year-out MSE.
The signal persists when previous-year demographic growth is added and becomes stronger when analysis is restricted to the four islands that remain extant.
The result is more specific than simple occupied-colony count: active colony count alone does not improve held-out-year prediction.
not_supported: a claim that the number of active colonies alone is a robust predictive mechanism
causal inference that terrestrial habitat loss caused next-year population decline
a claim that colony-code topology is an external habitat measurement
a claim that this small predictive gain explains the dominant long-term regional decline
ecological_interpretation: For these marine-foraging island breeders, the terrestrial signal appears in the internal distribution of breeders among subcolonies: populations spread more evenly across multiple breeding colonies retain slightly better next-year demographic performance than expected from current abundance and long-term decline alone. This is consistent with colony-network erosion as a local vulnerability state, but requires external spatial/topographic validation.
next_gate: Map colony codes to external spatial/topographic habitat information before making a causal habitat-fragmentation claim. Freeze any spatial validation design before opening colony coordinates or colony-specific habitat quality.
